payload.claim: Revisit on any of these: (1) the late-January 2027 board decision on the remaining KRW 55-75 trillion of 2026 returns. A large repurchase that is actually cancelled, enough to end the 3.6% annual net dilution, would improve the minority holder's claim; a program again held for stock compensation would confirm the governance concern. (2) Evidence on the memory cycle: if 2027 multi-year HBM/server DRAM contracts get disclosed terms and DS holds operating profit near Q3 2026 levels while announced industry capacity additions for late 2027-2028 slip, the peak-cycle objection weakens. Further NAND/DRAM spot declines, HBM margin cuts or share loss to SK Hynix/Micron/Chinese suppliers would strengthen it. (3) Cash conversion: FY2026 FCF/net income clearly above the 0.75 of FY2025 would answer the 0.3 four-year ratio. (4) Integrity gate escalation from Flag, or adverse final rulings on the roughly USD 1.06B of US patent verdicts and the ~USD 601M Indian customs demand. (5) A code-computed margin of safety that turns positive across the measured discount-rate range once the annual figures include FY2026.

prediction.reasoning: The bear case dates a supply cliff to 2028, with new capacity from late 2027, HBM margin compression and NAND spot already softening, and the business has a Weak cost-advantage moat and about 5.9x downside operating leverage. So I expect the full-year EBIT margin to fall well back from the Q3 2026 run-rate (KRW 107.4T operating profit on KRW 195.3T revenue) toward the 13.07% of FY2025. The price, which implies 32% annual growth for ten years, treats those peak earnings as durable. Cycle timing is uncertain, so confidence is low.
